title: A v1 create-contract authorization signed over its own bytes fails verification
pattern: HOST_FUNCTION_TYPE_CREATE_CONTRACT authorized by address credentials, root SOROBAN_AUTHORIZED_FUNCTION_TYPE_CREATE_CONTRACT_HOST_FN, signed over the entry's own bytes, as js-stellar-base's authorizeEntry signs it. The host reads the arm into its V2 form and hashes the signature payload from the V2 rendering (soroban-env-host auth.rs), so ed25519 verification fails and the call traps. This is by design since protocol 22: the host keeps one valid payload per action (github.com/orgs/stellar/discussions/1501). Transactions built through RPC simulation carry the V2 payload; offline signers must sign the V2 rendering.

hazards.placement: a v1 create authorization signed over its own bytes: verification fails

facts.says: The auth entry's root is the v1 create-contract function, for the kit Wasm.
With diagnostic events: crypto invalid_input, "failed ED25519 verification".
